title: Hepatoprotective effects of neohesperidin against acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury through modulation of EGFR signaling.
authors: Lai, Shanglei; Fu, Ai; Dong, Fan; Yu, Jundi; Wang, Keyi; Zeng, Yibo; Ding, Bin; Yu, Wangqin; Ding, Qinchao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究新橙皮苷对乙酰氨基酚肝损伤的保护作用，聚焦EGFR信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is a major cause of acute liver injury (ALI), yet effective therapies remain limited. Neohesperidin (Neo), a citrus-derived flavonoid glycoside, has recognized antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, but its role in APAP-induced hepatotoxicity is unclear. Here, APAP-induced ALI mice and APAP-treated AML12 hepatocytes were used to evaluate the hepatoprotective effects of Neo. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were performed to explore potential targets, and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling was further examined using pharmacological activation and gene silencing. Neo markedly alleviated APAP-induced liver injury, as shown by reduced alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, improved histopathology, and enhanced hepatocyte viability. Neo also restored redox homeostasis, increased antioxidant enzyme activities, reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, attenuated inflammatory responses, and suppressed endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via the protein kinase R-like ER kinase (PERK)- activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) pathway. Mechanistically, EGFR was identified as a potential target associated with Neo-mediated protection. Neo reduced APAP-induced EGFR phosphorylation in vivo and in vitro, whereas EGFR activation largely abolished its protective effects. EGFR silencing also alleviated APAP-induced hepatocyte injury. Overall, Neo protects against APAP-induced ALI, at least partly through modulation of EGFR signaling, accompanied by attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and ER stress.
abstract_zh: 对乙酰氨基酚（APAP）过量是急性肝损伤（ALI）的主要原因，然而有效的治疗方法仍然有限。新橙皮苷（Neo），一种源自柑橘类黄酮糖苷，具有公认的抗氧化和抗炎活性，但其在APAP诱导的肝毒性中的作用尚不清楚。本研究使用APAP诱导的ALI小鼠和APAP处理的AML12肝细胞来评估Neo的保肝作用。通过网络药理学和分子对接 (molecular docking) 探索潜在靶点，并利用药理学激活和基因沉默进一步检测表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）信号通路。Neo显著缓解了APAP诱导的肝损伤，表现为丙氨酸氨基转移酶（ALT）和天冬氨酸氨基转移酶（AST）水平降低、组织病理学改善以及肝细胞活力增强。Neo还恢复了氧化还原稳态，增加了抗氧化酶活性，减少了活性氧积累，减轻了炎症反应，并通过蛋白激酶R样内质网激酶（PERK）-激活转录因子4（ATF4）通路抑制了内质网（ER）应激。机制上，EGFR被确定为与Neo介导的保护作用相关的潜在靶点。Neo在体内和体外均降低了APAP诱导的EGFR磷酸化，而EGFR激活则基本消除了其保护作用。EGFR沉默也减轻了APAP诱导的肝细胞损伤。总体而言，Neo通过至少部分调节EGFR信号通路，并伴随减轻氧化应激、炎症和ER应激，来保护免受APAP诱导的ALI。
